result.title: Handoff Curves: Initial Selection, Later Handoff, and Supervision Targets in Multi-turn LLM Routing
result.summary: We study how initial model selection, later handoff, and training targets affect success and cost in LLM tasks that span multiple turns. We compare several router architectures using handoff curves, which record task success and cost as the handoff step changes. Our dataset contains 34,204 complete executions of three Qwen models across BFCL, MultiWOZ, and $τ$-retail, providing offline supervision for routing decisions. In our primary comparison, with Qwen3.5 35B-A3B as the starting model, allowing a later handoff does not establish an improvement in utility over initial selection on BFCL or MultiWOZ, and increases cost on BFCL across a range of cost weights. Changing the supervision targets improves router performance on both our dataset and TwinRouterBench. On our dataset, replacing noisy training success curves with monotone fits raises success by 0.2 to 4.1 percentage points at the same cost across the reported operating points. On TwinRouterBench, we construct targets that describe the model capability needed for the remaining work and difficult steps ahead. Compared with training on the benchmark's per-step labels, these targets raise trajectory pass scores by 7.8 percentage points and cost savings by 6.3 percentage points on the full static bank. A live deployment of the router trained with these targets resolves 79 of 100 instances at a router cost of 0.59 US dollars per instance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究多轮 LLM 任务中的路由决策，用「handoff 曲线」比较初始选型与中途切换模型对成功率与成本的影响，并考察不同监督目标（如单调拟合的成功曲线、描述剩余工作所需能力的标签）对训练路由器的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「何时切换/停止」的效用-成本权衡与噪声监督目标设计，可能与 LVR 中 STOP 决策的收益评估及轨迹监督信号构造形成类比，可供核查，但对象是模型间路由而非 latent 推理状态。
